record.title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD
record.titleEn: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD
record.description: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD remasters the Wii-era adventure that explores the origin of the Master Sword and the earliest known era of Zelda lore. This version sharpens the visuals, adds quality-of-life improvements, and supports both motion controls and button-only controls. Its structure leans more toward classic dungeons, item-based progression, and puzzle-driven exploration than the open-air Zelda entries.

Its structure leans more toward classic dungeons, item-based progression, and puzzle-driven exploration than the open-air Zelda entries.

contents.label: HD remaster of the Wii title

gameplayPillars.title: Classic dungeon progression
gameplayPillars.description: Skyward Sword HD places strong emphasis on directed progression through themed dungeons and item-based exploration.

gameplayPillars.title: Swordplay and motion controls
gameplayPillars.description: The combat system was originally built around directional sword attacks and still supports motion-driven play on Switch.

gameplayPillars.title: Button-only alternative controls
gameplayPillars.description: Nintendo added a non-motion control scheme that makes the game more comfortable for portable and traditional controller play.

gameplayPillars.title: Origin story of the Master Sword
gameplayPillars.description: The narrative explores the beginnings of iconic Zelda lore and the relationship between Link, Zelda, and Fi.

gameplayPillars.title: Puzzle-focused structure
gameplayPillars.description: Environmental riddles, dungeon mechanisms, and item usage are central to the game's identity.

record.worldSummary: Unlike the open-air Zelda entries, Skyward Sword HD emphasizes a more traditional adventure structure built around the sky hub, surface regions, dungeons, and story-driven progression.

storyChapters.title: Life above the clouds
storyChapters.body: Link begins his journey on Skyloft, a floating settlement in the sky where everyday life seems peaceful.

storyChapters.title: Descend to the surface
storyChapters.body: After Zelda is swept below, Link must travel to the dangerous world beneath the clouds to begin the rescue mission.

storyChapters.title: Forge the Master Sword
storyChapters.body: The quest becomes a foundational Zelda tale as Link strengthens the Goddess Sword and advances toward its legendary form.

storyChapters.title: Confront ancient evil
storyChapters.body: Classic Zelda dungeons and bosses gradually push the story toward the source of the kingdom's danger.

storyChapters.title: Resolve the origin-era conflict
storyChapters.body: The ending ties together the series' oldest mythology and the emotional stakes around Link and Zelda.

features: Traditional Zelda dungeon and item structure
Supports motion controls and button-only controls
Improved visuals and quality-of-life upgrades
Important lore about the origin of the Master Sword
Good fit for players who prefer classic Zelda design

faq.q: Does Skyward Sword HD support button-only controls?
faq.a: Yes. The HD release added a full button-control option in addition to the motion-control scheme.

faq.q: Is multiplayer supported?
faq.a: No. Skyward Sword HD is a single-player adventure.

faq.q: Is it related to Breath of the Wild in gameplay style?
faq.a: Not directly. Skyward Sword HD is much more structured and dungeon-driven than Nintendo's open-air Zelda titles.

faq.q: Why is this game important to Zelda lore?
faq.a: It tells an origin-era story about the Master Sword and major themes that echo throughout the series.

faq.q: Does it run well on Switch?
faq.a: Yes. The HD release targets 60 fps and is widely regarded as technically smoother than the original Wii version.

verdictPros: Strong classic Zelda dungeon design
60 fps presentation feels smooth
Button-only controls improve accessibility
Important lore and memorable boss encounters
Good remaster of a previously divisive game
verdictCons: Backtracking can feel repetitive
Motion controls remain imperfect for some players
Less freedom than modern open-world Zelda games
Early pacing is slower than some later entries
World structure is more segmented than expansive

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom

record.title: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
record.titleEn: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
record.description: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom builds on Breath of the Wild with a larger and denser version of Hyrule that now spans the surface, the sky, and the mysterious Depths below. Link gains abilities such as Ultrahand, Fuse, Ascend, and Recall, enabling players to build vehicles, combine equipment creatively, and solve problems in highly flexible ways. It is one of Nintendo's most ambitious adventure games.
record.descriptionEn: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom builds on Breath of the Wild with a larger and denser version of Hyrule that now spans the surface, the sky, and the mysterious Depths below. Link gains abilities such as Ultrahand, Fuse, Ascend, and Recall, enabling players to build vehicles, combine equipment creatively, and solve problems in highly flexible ways. It is one of Nintendo's most ambitious adventure games.

gameplayPillars.title: Ultrahand building
gameplayPillars.description: Players can assemble vehicles, machines, and problem-solving contraptions using a flexible construction system.

gameplayPillars.title: Fuse experimentation
gameplayPillars.description: Weapons, shields, and arrows can be fused with items and monster materials, dramatically expanding combat options.

gameplayPillars.title: Three-layer world design
gameplayPillars.description: The surface, sky islands, and underground Depths create a much more vertical adventure space than the previous game.

gameplayPillars.title: Open-ended puzzle solving
gameplayPillars.description: Ascend, Recall, and physics systems allow players to solve shrines, traversal problems, and combat scenarios creatively.

gameplayPillars.title: Epic main quest progression
gameplayPillars.description: Regional stories, major dungeons, and a powerful late-game arc make the sequel feel more directed while keeping openness intact.

record.worldSummary: Tears of the Kingdom takes Hyrule in three directions at once: upward into floating islands, downward into a shadowy underground realm, and deeper across the original surface world through more systems and secrets.

storyChapters.title: Investigate the Upheaval
storyChapters.body: Link and Zelda uncover a disaster beneath Hyrule Castle, setting in motion a crisis that reshapes the entire kingdom.

storyChapters.title: Master new powers
storyChapters.body: Ultrahand, Fuse, Ascend, and Recall define the sequel's structure and let players overcome obstacles in highly creative ways.

storyChapters.title: Travel across regions and temples
storyChapters.body: Each major region offers its own story arc, hazards, allies, and dungeon-like objectives tied to the central quest.

storyChapters.title: Explore the skies and the Depths
storyChapters.body: The sequel constantly expands its sense of discovery by layering additional spaces above and below Hyrule.

storyChapters.title: Resolve the fate of Hyrule
storyChapters.body: The story ultimately delivers a larger-scale finale with strong emotional stakes and memorable late-game revelations.

features: Massive expansion of Breath of the Wild's formula
Ultrahand and Fuse redefine traversal and combat creativity
Three-layer world structure greatly increases exploration depth
Large-scale dungeons and regional quest arcs
One of the highest-rated adventure games on Nintendo Switch

faq.q: Is this the original Nintendo Switch version?
faq.a: Yes. This file is for the original Nintendo Switch release of Tears of the Kingdom, not the separate Nintendo Switch 2 Edition.

faq.q: Does the game have DLC?
faq.a: No official standalone DLC has been announced for Tears of the Kingdom. This extraction therefore keeps only the base game variants.

faq.q: Is multiplayer supported?
faq.a: No. Tears of the Kingdom is a single-player adventure.

faq.q: What makes the sequel different from Breath of the Wild?
faq.a: The new abilities, layered world design, denser quest structure, and construction systems create a much more experimental sequel.

faq.q: Why is the game so popular?
faq.a: Its sense of discovery, creative problem solving, and ambitious expansion of open-world Zelda design have been praised almost universally.

verdictPros: Exceptional creativity tools
Dense and expansive world design
Outstanding sense of discovery
Regional arcs and dungeons add structure
Long-term exploration remains consistently rewarding
verdictCons: 30 fps target on original Switch hardware
Building systems can feel overwhelming at first
Inventory and material management can get busy
Some puzzle solutions can trivialize challenge if over-optimized
Huge scale can extend completion time significantly

faq.q: Does the Switch Complete Edition include both major expansions?
faq.a: Yes. The Complete Edition includes Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine along with the base game and released DLC.

faq.q: Is this the new Switch 2 Remastered version?
faq.a: No. This file is for the original Nintendo Switch Complete Edition. The 2026 native Switch 2 Remastered release is separate.

faq.q: Can save data be moved to other platforms?
faq.a: Later updates added cross-save support with supported PC ecosystems.

faq.q: Is the game multiplayer?
faq.a: No. The Witcher 3 is a single-player RPG.

faq.q: How compromised is the Switch version?
faq.a: It uses reduced resolution and visual settings relative to more powerful platforms, but preserves the complete gameplay and story package.

faq.q: When does the Switch 2 Remastered version release?
faq.a: September 29, 2026, according to CD PROJEKT RED’s official announcement.

faq.q: Is this just backward compatibility?
faq.a: No. CD PROJEKT RED explicitly announced a native Nintendo Switch 2 version of Remastered.

faq.q: Are exact resolution and FPS values confirmed?
faq.a: Not yet. They are intentionally marked Not Announced in this file rather than estimated.

faq.q: Does it include the classic expansions?
faq.a: CD PROJEKT RED’s Remastered ecosystem modernizes the base game and its first two expansions, and existing owners were granted access to Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine.

faq.q: What is Songs of the Past?
faq.a: It is a newly announced paid expansion planned for 2027, featuring the new region of Letten.
